title: Storage Private Endpoints
description: Connect to Azure Storage privately over a virtual network using private endpoints instead of public endpoints.

data.text: A **private endpoint** is a network interface that maps a private IP address from your virtual network to an Azure Storage account. Traffic between your VNet and the storage account travels over the Azure backbone network, never touching the public internet. This is essential for compliance-sensitive workloads and zero-trust architectures.

When you enable a private endpoint, the storage account still has a public endpoint, but you can disable public network access entirely. This forces all traffic through the private endpoint, which is only reachable from your virtual network.

You create a private endpoint from the storage account's Networking blade. You choose a virtual network and subnet, and optionally integrate with private DNS so the storage endpoint resolves to the private IP automatically.

data.title: Create a Private Endpoint with Azure CLI
data.content: Add a private endpoint for blob service in a VNet
data.code:
az network private-endpoint create \
  --name pe-storage-blob \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --vnet-name myVnet \
  --subnet mySubnet \
  --private-connection-resource-id $(az storage account show -n stdemostorage -g rg-demo --query id -o tsv) \
  --group-id blob \
  --connection-name conn-storage-blob

data.title: Disable Public Network Access with PowerShell
data.content: Block all public traffic to the storage account

terms.definition: A network interface that connects a PaaS resource privately to a virtual network using a private IP address.
An Azure DNS zone that resolves a storage endpoint name to its private IP address within a VNet.
A setting on storage accounts that allows or blocks traffic from public endpoints.

data.title: DNS Is Critical
data.text: After creating a private endpoint, your applications must resolve the storage URL to the private IP. Use Azure Private DNS zones or custom DNS servers to ensure the correct resolution.

data.title: Exercise: Connect Privately to Storage
data.description: Create a private endpoint, update DNS, and verify access.
steps: Create a private endpoint for blob service in your storage account.
Create or link a private DNS zone named 'privatelink.blob.core.windows.net'.
Disable public network access on the storage account.
From a VM in the same VNet, resolve the blob endpoint and confirm it returns the private IP.
Upload a blob from the VM and confirm it succeeds.
data.expectedOutcome: A VM that reaches the storage account only through the private endpoint with no public exposure.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Private endpoints map storage services to private VNet IP addresses.
Traffic stays on the Azure backbone and never reaches the public internet.
Private DNS zones ensure applications resolve to the private IP.
Disabling public access enforces zero-trust storage access.
data.takeaway: Private endpoints are the foundation of secure, compliant, zero-trust storage architectures.
